dedupe_keys.name: cdc forecast hubs flusight covid 19 rsv weekly ensemble and team forecasts of us hospital admissions

description: The CDC forecast hubs collect probabilistic forecasts of respiratory disease burden from dozens of modelling teams each week and publish them with a CDC ensemble. They are run by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on the hubverse standard of the Consortium of Infectious Disease Modeling Hubs. Coverage: the United States, national level plus all 50 states, Washington DC and Puerto Rico; the FluSight hub has run each influenza season (the 2026-2027 challenge starts on 7 October 2026 and runs to May), with separate hubs for COVID-19 and RSV. Teams submit quantile nowcasts and forecasts of weekly laboratory-confirmed hospital admissions and the share of emergency department visits for the previous, current and next three weeks, together with model metadata; the repositories also hold target data and ensemble outputs. Format and access: CSV and Parquet model output files with YAML metadata in public GitHub repositories, free to download. Licence: MIT for the repository; CDC asks users to contact it about attribution of individual teams' forecasts. Caveats: forecasts are submitted in real time and target data are revised, team participation varies by week, and skill drops beyond two weeks ahead. Simulation uses: hospital demand scenarios for capacity planning and emergency response of healthcare services during epidemic seasons. Related records: hubverse (platform-hubverse-modeling-hub-tools) supplies the data standards and tools, and the Rush COVID-19 hospital needs forecaster (model-rush-covid-hospital-needs-forecaster) turns such forecasts into bed demand.
